data.text: XR technologies have huge application potential in many domains. AR does not require an immersive experience and instead emphasizes augmenting real-world content with digital content. Applications include reconstructing lost structures, troubleshooting industrial components, and providing one motivation for the metaverse through commerce.

data.text: AR can be used to help users navigate large terminals and to preview products or measure objects in physical spaces. It also offers virtual try-on experiences for various products. Additionally, AR supports healthcare through training, telemedicine, and the visualization of internal structures.
points: AR can help users navigate large terminals by showing exact locations and directions.
AR allows for virtual product previews and measuring objects in physical spaces.
AR provides virtual try-on experiences for various products.
AR is used in healthcare for training, telemedicine, and visualizing internal structures.

data.text: Augmented reality applications are categorized into marker-based and markerless systems. Marker-based applications trigger content at specific markers but can be difficult to maintain, whereas markerless applications are more versatile and allow users to decide where to place virtual objects. Markerless systems include location-based, superimposition-based, projection-based, and outlining-based subcategories that use sensors, computer vision, and projectors to augment the real-world view.
points: AR applications are categorized into marker-based and markerless systems.
Marker-based applications trigger content at specific markers but can be difficult to maintain.
Markerless applications are more versatile and allow users to decide where to place virtual objects.
Markerless systems include location-based, superimposition-based, projection-based, and outlining-based subcategories.
These subtypes use location sensors, object recognition, or light projectors to augment the real-world view.

data.text: VR systems are categorized by psychological experience into non-immersive, semi-immersive, and fully immersive systems, while AR systems are categorized by technology into marker-based and markerless systems. Markerless AR techniques rely on computer vision and other sensors to overcome the difficulty of maintaining markers. While VR and AR have similar application domains, VR is characterized as immersive and AR emphasizes augmenting digital content onto the real-world view.
points: VR systems are categorized by psychological experience into non-immersive, semi-immersive, and fully immersive systems.
AR systems are categorized by technology into marker-based and markerless systems.
Markerless AR techniques rely on computer vision and other sensors to overcome the difficulty of maintaining markers.
VR is characterized as immersive while AR emphasizes augmenting digital content onto the real-world view.
